title: The single-complex stalk condition on etale scheme charts
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], with derived pullback computed by K-flat resolutions with flat terms and derived direct image by K-injective resolutions. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms, $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $g',f'$, and $\phi:L(g')^*K\to K'$ for $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'})$. At a geometric point $\bar z$ of $X'$, put $\bar x=g'\bar z$, $\bar y'=f'\bar z$, $\bar y=f\bar x$, and $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X',\bar z}$. Define the geometric stalk condition by requiring that every canonical map
$$H^i(K_{\bar x}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_{A\otimes_RB}C\longrightarrow H^i(K'_{\bar z})$$
is an isomorphism, for every $\bar z$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$. The map is induced by the scalar-extension comparison $K_{\bar x}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to K_{\bar x}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C\to K'_{\bar z}$, the second arrow coming from $\phi$, followed by $C$-linear extension on cohomology.
This condition is equivalent to the following chart condition. For every commutative diagram of schemes $U\to V$, $V'\to V$ over $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, with etale maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, $c:V'\to Y'$, set $U'=U\times_VV'$. Transport $a^*K$, $K'|_{U'}$, and the induced coefficient map to the Zariski derived categories using the canonical equivalences [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], obtaining $K_U,K'_{U'}$ and $\phi_U$. For every ordinary point $z\in U'$ and every integer $i$, put $x=g'_U(z)$, $v'=f'_U(z)$, $v=f_U(x)$; then the map
$$H^i((K_U)_x\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{V,v}}\mathcal O_{V',v'})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{U,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{V,v}}\mathcal O_{V',v'}}\mathcal O_{U',z}\longrightarrow H^i((K'_{U'})_z)$$
is an isomorphism. It is precisely the canonical ordinary single-complex comparison [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. The geometric stalk condition is preserved by restricting $X$ to an etale algebraic space over $X$, by etale base change on $Y$, and by etale restriction on $Y'$. When all four spaces are schemes, it is equivalent to this ordinary Zariski stalk condition for the corresponding complexes. No quasi-compactness, boundedness, or flatness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Fix a diagram of charts from the statement. The map $q:U'=U\times_VV'\to X'$ is etale: factor it through $U\times_YV'$. The first factor is the base change of the etale diagonal $V\to V\times_YV$, and the second is the composite of the base changes of $U\to X$ and $V'\to Y'$. The diagonal is etale because it is a morphism over $V$ between the etale $V$-schemes $V$ and $V\times_YV$. The scheme-test and permanence assertions cited below justify all these claims. At a geometric point of $U'$, etale localization identifies its four geometric local rings with those on $X,Y,Y',X'$; the ring maps agree. Ringed chart localization and derived pullback composition identify the restricted coefficient morphism with the chart coefficient morphism. Thus the two geometric comparison maps are the same: on tensor representatives both use the given coefficient morphism after multiplying the scalar factors.

source.place: Tag 0DKG (lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition), proof and equation-bc immediately preceding it.

proof.text:
Work now on the scheme square $U'\to U$, $V'\to V$. The derived etale--Zariski equivalence supplies $K_U,K'_{U'}$ and carries their coefficient morphism to the specified etale one. Fix $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U'$ and its images $\bar x,\bar v',\bar v$. Write $r,a,b,c$ for the ordinary local rings at $v,x,v',z$, and $\widetilde r,\widetilde a,\widetilde b,\widetilde c$ for their geometric local rings. They are the compatible strict henselizations. The natural module stalk formula, applied termwise, identifies
$$K_{\bar x}\simeq (K_U)_x\otimes_a^{\mathbf L}\widetilde a,\qquad K'_{\bar z}\simeq (K'_{U'})_z\otimes_c^{\mathbf L}\widetilde c.$$
Indeed the scalar extensions are flat by faithful flatness of strict henselization, so ordinary tensor already computes derived tensor and commutes with cohomology (apply the flat-tensor lemma on the one-point ringed site). The stalk formula is natural for every module map; the resulting complex identifications therefore also identify the coefficient morphism, with the pullback comparison fixed in the derived equivalence. No boundedness is used.

source.place: Tag 0DKG (lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition), proof and equation-bc immediately preceding it.

proof.text:
Apply the strict-local refinement lemma to the local maps $r\to a$ and $r\to b$, using the residue embeddings determined by the common field $\Omega$. It gives flatness of $a\otimes_r\widetilde r\to\widetilde a$ and $\widetilde r\otimes_r b\to\widetilde b$; $r\to\widetilde r$ is faithfully flat. Put $d=a\otimes_r b$ and $\widetilde d=\widetilde a\otimes_{\widetilde r}\widetilde b$. The flat ring-diagram comparison, with $M=(K_U)_x$, consequently gives the canonical isomorphism
$$H^i(K_{\bar x}\otimes_{\widetilde r}^{\mathbf L}\widetilde b)\cong H^i((K_U)_x\otimes_r^{\mathbf L}b)\otimes_d\widetilde d.$$
All three flatness hypotheses of that comparison have just been checked. This is an identification of cohomology modules with their two commuting ring actions, not an assumption of Tor independence of $U$ and $V'$ over $V$.

source.place: Tag 0DKG (lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition), proof and equation-bc immediately preceding it.

proof.text: Extend the last isomorphism along $\widetilde d\to\widetilde c$. Tensor associativity identifies the geometric source with $H^i((K_U)_x\otimes_r^{\mathbf L}b)\otimes_d\widetilde c$. On the target, the flat-tensor cohomology comparison identifies $H^i(K'_{\bar z})$ with $H^i((K'_{U'})_z)\otimes_c\widetilde c$. Under these identifications the geometric arrow is precisely the ordinary comparison tensored with $\widetilde c$ over $c$. To check the arrow, choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ and a K-injective target $N$ representing the coefficient map by $t$. Use a free $r$-resolution of $b$ for the base-derived tensor. Its augmentation, followed by $t_z$, sends a representative with factors $p,b_0$ and final scalar $s$ to $s\,t_z(p\otimes b_0)$. Extending the scalars through $\widetilde r,\widetilde a,\widetilde b$ gives the identical formula with the product of the inserted scalars. The comparison of the previous step respects these augmentations, and the etale--Zariski comparison respects scalar insertion; hence the square commutes. Since $c\to\widetilde c$ is faithfully flat, the arrows are isomorphisms simultaneously: reflect exactness of the two triples $0\to\mathrm{source}\to\mathrm{target}$ and $\mathrm{source}\to\mathrm{target}\to0$. This proves the scheme ordinary/geometric equivalence point by point; every ordinary point has a geometric point above it.

source.place: Tag 0DKG (lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition), proof and equation-bc immediately preceding it.

proof.text: If the global geometric condition holds, step 1 gives it on every chart square, and steps 2--4 give the stated ordinary condition. Conversely fix $\bar z$ on $X'$. Choose an etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and lift its image to $V$; choose an atlas $U\to X\times_YV$ and lift the pair $(\bar x,\bar v)$; choose an atlas $V'\to Y'\times_YV$ and lift $(\bar y',\bar v)$. The algebraic-space definition supplies the atlases, fibre-product covering and representable-etale permanence make their composites etale, and the specified-point lifting lemma supplies the lifts over the same $\Omega$. They give a lift of $\bar z$ to $U\times_VV'$. The ordinary chart hypothesis implies the geometric comparison is invertible there by steps 2--4, and step 1 identifies it with the comparison at $\bar z$. Thus it is invertible globally. In the scheme case use identity charts to obtain the ordinary condition, and the converse follows already from steps 2--4.

source.place: Tag 0DKG (lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition), proof and equation-bc immediately preceding it.

proof.text: Finally restrict $X$ etale, base change $Y$ etale, or restrict $Y'$ etale, pulling back the two complexes and the coefficient morphism. The resulting maps on the four vertices are etale, by the same permanence assertions. Their geometric local rings and all structural ring maps identify with the original ones by etale localization. Pullback composition identifies the coefficient morphisms; both comparison arrows are therefore still given by the scalar multiplication and coefficient-map formula in step 1. Each restricted comparison is an original comparison, so invertibility is preserved. This proves all three preservation assertions without a quasi-compactness, boundedness, or flatness hypothesis on $f$ or $g$.
